debate.why: Piers Morgan and two guests argue against Andrew Wilson over whether the Fort Hood shooter's firing squad execution should be livestreamed, and they rebut and interrupt each other directly.

exchanges.motion: Should we have seen how Bin Laden was shot?
exchanges.a_side: Hiding the killing avoided fuelling martyrdom
exchanges.b_side: Hiding the killing fuelled conspiracy theories
exchanges.hook_topic: on how Bin Laden was shot
exchanges.take_hook: Should we have *seen* Bin Laden die?
exchanges.retention: The opening line, "We never saw how Bin Laden was shot," hooks anyone who remembers that raid. Piers says hiding it stopped martyrdom, and that holds until Andrew comes back with the claim that the secrecy made people doubt SEAL Team 6 killed him at all.

exchanges.motion: Is killing prisoners on camera murder?
exchanges.a_side: Killing prisoners on camera is murder
exchanges.b_side: Murder is unjustified killing, so this isn't murder
exchanges.retention: The opening, "Christian right-wing fundamentalist lunatics murdering their prisoners on camera," stops the scroll. Andrew's "That's not murder" leaves open what the word even means, and his last line settles it with his definition.

exchanges.motion: Should fear of terrorists stop us doing something just?
exchanges.a_side: Don't give up just policy over terrorists' reaction
exchanges.b_side: Don't give terrorists an excuse for their crazy
exchanges.retention: The opening, "We're supposed to cede something that's just because then terrorists will do something," sets up a clear clash. Piers pushes back that it's about not giving them an excuse, and Andrew's last line turns that exact point back on him.
